view.headline: Curve bull-steepens as 2Y sheds 3.5bp into Friday's payroll, gold rips to $4,486 — and Broadcom's soft Q4 guide sinks it 3% against a green SMH tape, the tell that the AI-capex bar has outrun even the winners.

schedule.event: Fed's Hammack (Cleveland) & Goolsbee (Chicago) special remarks, 'Connecting Communities' online event

sections.body: The 2Y sits at 4.336% (−3.5bp) and the 10Y at 4.752% (−2.8bp) on TradingView's live curve (ow_macro_rates liveNow, fetchedAt 2026-09-03T17:00:20.911Z). The front end is leading the rally, so the 2s10s steepens to +41.6bp — a bull-steepener the day before payrolls, the front end pulling down harder than the belly. Note the shape is inverted-turned-positive at the long end: the 30Y at 5.234% (−2.6bp) sits well above the 10Y. This is the 'good' direction for duration — everything is richer — but the level still bites. Rank by cash-flow duration, from most-helped-to-most-exposed: the longest-duration equity — unprofitable-until-2030 growth, the crypto-treasury and small-cap complex (IWM +0.98 to 294.99) — gets the biggest present-value tailwind from lower discount rates and is why the front-end rally matters; long-bond proxies (TLT 82.325, +0.375) get a direct mark-up; mega-cap tech (QQQ +8.38) rides it comfortably. The hurt is muted today because rates fell across the whole curve — but the 30Y above 5.2% is the reminder that the term-premium floor under long-duration cash flows has not moved.
sections.title: Rates are the first cause

sections.body: Broadcom. AVGO trades 356.37, down −10.87 (~−3%), while the entire semi and mega-cap tape it anchors is green: SMH's sector complex bid, NVDA +3.07 to 227.48, MRVL +5.27 to 211.75, ALAB +5.60 to 279.73, XLK +2.25 to 185.845, QQQ +8.38. A name falling 3% inside a rallying group it is a bellwether of is the anomaly. The cause is the expectations bar, not sentiment: Broadcom did not miss on the print, it guided the top line light. Per Unusual Whales, 2026-09-02T20:17:34Z — 'BROADCOM SEES 4Q REV. ABOUT $34.8B, EST. $35.05B' — and 2026-09-02T20:20:20Z — 'BROADCOM TUMBLES 6.8% AFTER 4Q REVENUE OUTLOOK MISSES ESTIMATE.' The bar for the AI-infrastructure leaders is now set at beat-AND-raise; a merely-in-line-to-soft revenue outlook, against a stock that had front-run tens of billions of AI chip financing, is enough to sink it while its peers rally on the same AI-capex thesis. The sell-side confirms the re-rate: Unusual Whales, 2026-09-03T13:40:29Z — 'BofA Global Research cuts Broadcom's price objective to $460 from $530.' The divergence is the market marking down the marginal dollar of AI revenue at the one name where the expectations bar had climbed highest.
sections.title: Today's largest divergence

sections.body: No clean beat-and-raise-that-closed-down name surfaces in today's coverage. The one large decliner into a green tape, Broadcom, is a guide-DOWN (Q4 revenue outlook of ~$34.8B below the ~$35.05B estimate, per Unusual Whales 2026-09-02T20:17:34Z), not a beat-and-raise — so it does not carry this tag; it is treated as the divergence above. Absent a beat-and-raise print marked down today, the pricing-power-exhausted signal does not fire. Flagging the absence rather than forcing a name onto the tag: the tell to watch tomorrow is whether an in-line-or-better payroll fails to lift the long-duration complex.
sections.title: Good news, priced down = pricing power exhausted

sections.body: Two Fed voices are dated for today — Cleveland's Hammack and Chicago's Goolsbee, 'Connecting Communities' remarks at 2026-09-03T19:00:00Z (ow_uw_calendar, asOf 2026-09-03T17:00:23.127Z) — but the reaction is read off the tape, not guessed forward. What the front end is already pricing: the futures-implied path (ow_argon_policy_path, Frenzy Capital fed-funds futures via argon, snapshot 2026-09-02 — futures-implied via Frenzy Capital, NOT CME FedWatch) has the 9/16 meeting at a 60% HIKE / 40% Hold, implied rate 3.78%, target 3.75–4.00%; then 10/28 leaning HOLD at 70%; then 12/9 back to a 64% HIKE. That is a market pricing a Fed still in a tightening-bias reaction function — the input that matters is inflation/labor running hot enough to justify hikes, not cuts. Yet today the 2Y richened 3.5bp and the curve bull-steepened, and gold ripped +2.23% to $4,486 with silver +2.53% and DXY −0.71 to 98.864 (ow_tv_commodities, asOf 2026-09-03T17:00:26.278Z; ow_macro_rates liveNow) — a real-asset, weaker-dollar bid that reads as the market fading the hike-path stiffness ahead of tomorrow's 08:30 ET payroll (consensus +50k jobs, prior −23k; unemployment 4.1% vs 4.1% prior; AHE +0.2% m/m). The reaction function in one line: the front end says a soft labor print pulls the September hike odds down fast, and the gold/dollar move is the early vote for that.
